title: Korean greetings and Hangul
examples: How do I say hello in Korean?
What is Hangul and how do I read it?
Can you teach me a few basic Korean phrases?

explain.say: Today we are learning some Korean words and letters. We will learn how to say hello in Korean.
The word for hello is annyeonghaseyo. You can use this when greeting people.
Korean writing uses a special alphabet called Hangul. Hangul is very systematic to learn.
Hangul letters build syllables in blocks. A block always needs at least one consonant and one vowel.
Let us look at a simple syllable block. For example, the letters ㄱ and ㅏ make the syllable 가.
In real life, you see Hangul everywhere in Korea. Signs and street names use these blocks.

faq.a: King Sejong the Great created Hangul. He wanted everyone to be able to read and write easily.
Many people find it quite logical to learn. It is designed to be easy for people to pick up.
asks: Is it difficult to read Korean?
How long does it take to learn Hangul?

faq.q: What is the difference between Hangul and Chinese characters?
faq.a: Hangul is a phonetic alphabet designed for Korean sounds. Chinese characters are usually based on ideas or concepts.
asks: Are Korean letters like English letters?

faq.q: Do I need to learn all the letters to speak?
faq.a: No, knowing a few basic greetings is a great start. You can learn more letters later on.
asks: Can I speak Korean without knowing everything?
What is the most important thing to learn first?

faq.q: How do I say goodbye in Korean?
faq.a: You can learn to say goodbye later. For now, focusing on 'annyeonghaseyo' is perfect.
asks: What is the word for goodbye?
Are there different ways to say bye?

facts: Hangul is the native alphabet of the Korean language.
It was created by King Sejong the Great.
Korean syllables are written in square blocks.
The letters are designed to mimic the shape of the mouth when speaking.

quiz.say: What is the Korean word for 'hello'?
quiz.why: This is the standard greeting taught in Korean culture.

wrong.1: This phrase actually means 'please stay well' and is used when leaving.
wrong.2: This means 'thank you' and is used for gratitude.

quiz.say: How are Hangul letters grouped to form a syllable?
quiz.why: Syllables always combine at least one consonant and one vowel together.

wrong.0: A vowel alone is often used, but in writing, it usually needs a placeholder consonant.
wrong.1: Hangul is purely an alphabetic writing system, not a mix of numbers and letters.
wrong.3: A consonant alone cannot form a complete, pronounceable syllable block.

quiz.say: If you combine the consonant ㄱ and the vowel ㅏ, what syllable do you make?
quiz.why: The structure requires placing the consonant first, followed by the vowel to form the block.

wrong.0: The standard order in Korean syllable blocks is consonant first, then vowel.
wrong.1: This adds an extra vowel that does not belong in the basic combination.
wrong.3: Writing them separately like this does not form a single, correct syllable block.
